probe.recommendation:
probe: 72 heads removed (50%), accuracy 0.7844 -> 0.1790, 60.54pp lost
FRAGILE (drop > 30pp). One question decides the method, and it is not the band:
  can you fine-tune AFTER pruning?
    yes -> prune at random, then recover. This is the shipped path:
      compress(pruning=0.5, strategy='random', slice_heads=True)
      recover(train_dataset, epochs=2, domain=...)
    no  -> train with head masking first, with mask_mode='drophead':
      SALConfig.auto(model, prune_fraction=0.5, mask_mode='drophead')
      compress(pruning=0.5, slice_heads=True)
measured on ViT-B/16 / ImageNet-1k, 3 seeds, full 50k val split, against a dense control trained for the same 2 epochs (81.554%): at 50% of heads the one-shot model reads 9.56% and two epochs of recovery reach 78.816% with random selection (-2.738pp) or 77.642% with magnitude (-3.91pp). Head training is worth +0.05pp (SAL) or +0.07pp (DropHead) as a starting point for that recovery, i.e. nothing.
if you cannot recover: DropHead, with no exception. SAL's adaptation is worth +56.18pp on the one head set it trained for and 0 to 8pp on any other, and on that same own-set cell DropHead is +0.67pp above SAL on 3/3 seeds of a 631M encoder, so the "SAL when the deployed set is fixed" carve-out is withdrawn. SAL's own-set operating point is -3.93pp against the matched baseline at a 16.5% smaller model, which is the figure to compare, not its dense row.
then: head pruning is the small half of the compression, and FFN neurons are the cheaper structure. At the same 2 epochs of recovery and the same matched control, 25% of FFN neurons cost 0.869pp at -16.4% of parameters (7 seeds, range -0.988 to -0.664) against 2.738pp for 50% of heads at -16.5% (3 seeds), so heads are about three times more expensive per unit of size removed. Prune FFN neurons by MAGNITUDE, not at random: random costs 1.397pp on the same cell (7 seeds, range -1.668 to -1.212), and the two ranges do not overlap. The inversion worth knowing is that random is 1.91pp BETTER one-shot and 0.528pp worse after recovery, so a one-shot benchmark picks the wrong FFN default. Neuron pruning is not part of sal-torch; see ROADMAP.md.
finally: torch.compile. Measured 1.12x on a dense ViT-B/16 at batch 32 and 1.50x on a pruned one, and 2.2x at batch 1 where pruning alone buys almost nothing.
